text.en: The settings of py-words. Each setting can be left out (or the whole file deleted) to use its usual value. The program rewrites this file when settings are saved: the values are kept, but not comments of your own.
text.tr: Optiones programmatis py-words. Quelibet optio omitti potest (vel totus fasciculus deleri) ut valor eius consuetus adhibeatur. Programma hunc fasciculum rescribit cum optiones servantur: valores retinentur, sed non annotationes tue.

text.en: text_family and text_size: the results (a fixed-width font); ui_family and ui_size: the rest of the windows.
text.tr: text_family et text_size: inventa (typus litterarum latitudinis fixe); ui_family et ui_size: reliqua pars fenestrarum.

text.en: Where dictionary.xml and the other data files are; empty: the data folder next to the program. (--datadir and $PY_WORDS_DATADIR come first.)
text.tr: Ubi sint dictionary.xml et ceteri fasciculi datorum; vacuum: capsula data iuxta programma. (--datadir et $PY_WORDS_DATADIR priora sunt.)

text.en: The parameters (changed with # in interactive mode).
The developer modes and command characters (changed with ! in interactive mode).
text.tr: Modi elaboratoris et characteres mandatorum (mutantur per ! in modo interlocutorio).

text.en: The fonts of the windows (also changed with "Font…" and Ctrl and + or -). Sizes are in points.
text.tr: Typi litterarum fenestrarum (mutantur etiam per "Typi litterarum…" et Ctrl cum + vel -). Magnitudines sunt in punctis.

text.en: the entry is not in the dictionary
there is no meaning in {language}: the English one is shown
there is no entry to delete
{key} and + or − change all the sizes; {key} and 0 brings back the usual fonts.
text.tr: {key} cum + vel − omnes magnitudines mutat; {key} cum 0 typos consuetos reddit.

text.en: The developer modes (! in the command line), for special purposes.
text.tr: Modi elaboratoris (! in linea mandatorum), ad usus speciales.

text.en: Point at a setting to read more about it. Changes apply at once and are kept for next time.
text.tr: Murinum super optionem pone ut plura de ea legas. Mutationes statim valent et in posterum servantur.

text.en: “{value}” cannot be {setting}: it must be one punctuation character, different from the others and from ~.
text.tr: “{value}” non potest esse {setting}: debet esse unus character interpunctionis, diversus ab aliis et a ~.

text.en: Go back to the default value of every setting?
Forget the earlier searches (in the window and the command line)?
text.tr: Oblivisci inquisitionum priorum (in fenestra et in linea mandatorum)?

text.en: Only in the interactive command line
Do not try spelling tricks on an unknown word that is capitalized: it is probably a name.
text.tr: Noli artificia orthographie temptare in verbo ignoto quod a littera maiuscula incipit: probabiliter est nomen proprium.

text.en: Read a participle followed by a form of esse as a compound tense (laudatus est: perfect passive).
text.tr: Lege participium quod sequitur forma verbi esse tamquam tempus compositum (laudatus est: perfectum passivum).

text.en: When a word is not in the dictionary, try it as a known word with a prefix or suffix. The results may be less reliable than those found directly.
text.tr: Cum verbum non est in dictionario, tempta ipsum tamquam verbum notum cum prefixo vel suffixo. Inventa possunt esse minus certa quam ea que directe inveniuntur.

text.en: Show each entry with its principal parts and grammar (amicus, amici noun, 2nd declension, masculine).
text.tr: Ostende quemlibet articulum cum partibus principalibus et grammatica sua (amicus, amici noun, 2nd declension, masculine).

text.en: Write the analyses of the forms in glossing abbreviations, as in the Leipzig Glossing Rules (GEN.PL, 2SG.PRF.ACT.IND); if not, in words (genitive plural, 2nd person singular perfect active indicative). The abbreviations are those of data/gloss.xml.
text.tr: Scribe analyses formarum abbreviationibus glossarum, sicut in Leipzig Glossing Rules (GEN.PL, 2SG.PRF.ACT.IND); sin autem, verbis (genitive plural, 2nd person singular perfect active indicative). Abbreviationes sunt ille fasciculi data/gloss.xml.

text.en: Show only the entries and their meanings, without the forms.
text.tr: Ostende solos articulos et significationes eorum, sine formis.

text.en: For an unknown word, list the dictionary entries near where it would be. This can catch a word whose stem is in the dictionary under another part of speech.
text.tr: Pro verbo ignoto, enumera articulos dictionarii vicinos loco ubi esset. Sic inveniri potest verbum cuius radix est in dictionario sub alia parte orationis.

text.en: When a word finds nothing as it is typed, look for the words one change away from it (a letter left out, added or changed, or two letters swapped), and show the nearest three: amicuss finds amicus, and, in the search to Latin, freind finds friend and wolfs finds wolf. Exact results are shown as before.
text.tr: Cum verbum nichil invenit sicut scriptum est, quere verba que una mutatione ab ipso distant (una littera omissa, addita vel mutata, vel due littere permutate), et ostende tria proxima: amicuss invenit amicus, et, in inquisitione in Latinum, freind invenit friend et wolfs invenit wolf. Inventa exacta ostenduntur ut prius.

text.en: The language of the meanings, and of the rest of the results (en, es ...). The search to Latin is from this language.
text.tr: Lingua significationum, et ceterorum inventorum (en, es ...). Inquisitio in Latinum ab hac lingua incipit.

text.en: The language of the menus, buttons, messages and help of the programs (en, es, la).
text.tr: Lingua tabellarum, bullarum, nuntiorum et auxilii programmatum (en, es, la).

text.en: Save these settings in the configuration file, config.toml (on Linux in ~/.config/py-words), to be used at the next start. It is plain text and can also be edited; words.py --config shows where it is.
text.tr: Serva has optiones in fasciculo configurationis, config.toml (in Linux in ~/.config/py-words), ut proximo initio adhibeantur. Est textus simplex et etiam emendari potest; words.py --config ostendit ubi sit.

text.en: Show the codes of each entry: age, area, geography, frequency and source, as in [XXXBO].
text.tr: Ostende notas cuiuslibet articuli: etatem, materiam, regionem, frequentiam et fontem, sicut in [XXXBO].

text.en: Start each line of the results with a code saying what it is (01 a form, 02 an entry, 03 a meaning, 05 an affix, 06 a trick, 00 an unknown word), for programs that read the output.
text.tr: Incipe quamlibet lineam inventorum a nota que dicit quid sit (01 forma, 02 articulus, 03 significatio, 05 affixum, 06 artificium, 00 verbum ignotum), pro programmatibus que exitum legunt.

text.en: On the command line, in a terminal, show results longer than the screen in the pager (less, or $PAGER: PgUp and PgDn scroll, / finds, q goes back); where there is none, pause after each screenful in interactive use.
text.tr: In linea mandatorum, in terminali, ostende inventa longiora quam visus in paginatore (less, vel $PAGER: PgUp et PgDn movent, / querit, q redit); ubi nullus est, siste post quemlibet visum plenum in usu interlocutorio.

text.en: The characters that start a command at the beginning of a line: reading a file (@), the parameters (#) and the developer modes (!). They must be punctuation, and different from each other and from ~.
text.tr: Characteres qui mandatum incipiunt in principio linee: lectionem fasciculi (@), parametra (#) et modos elaboratoris (!). Debent esse signa interpunctionis, diversa inter se et a ~.

text.en: Use ~E for {language} to Latin, ~L for Latin to {language}
{language} to Latin: type a word in {language}, and optionally a part of speech (N, ADJ, V, PREP ...)
text.tr: {language} → Latine: scribe verbum {language}, et, si placet, partem orationis (N, ADJ, V, PREP ...)

text.en: {path} has errors ({problems}); the defaults are used for those lines
text.tr: {path} habet errores ({problems}); pro illis lineis valores primitivi adhibentur

text.tr: Completus est fasciculus configurationis {path}, cum optionibus que in usu sunt

text.tr: {key}: debet esse nota lingue, ut "en" vel "es"

text.en: Answer Y or N; Enter keeps the current value, ? gives help, a space skips the rest.
text.tr: Responde I (ita) vel N (non); Enter valorem presentem retinet, ? auxilium dat, spatium reliqua transit.

text.en: Answer Y or N; Enter keeps the current value, ? gives help, a space skips the rest. Developer modes are for special purposes.
text.tr: Responde I (ita) vel N (non); Enter valorem presentem retinet, ? auxilium dat, spatium reliqua transit. Modi elaboratoris sunt ad usus speciales.

text.en: Type a Latin word or line and Enter. ~E: {language} to Latin, ~L: back to Latin.
text.tr: Scribe verbum vel lineam Latinam et Enter. ~E: {language} → Latine, ~L: rursus a Latino.

text.en: {file}FILE: look up a file {parameters}: parameters {developer}: developer modes ?: commands ~H: help ~A: about
text.tr: {file}FASCICULUS: querere fasciculum {parameters}: parametra {developer}: modi elaboratoris ?: mandata ~H: auxilium ~A: de programmate
Linea vacua bis scripta programma claudit.

text.en: Type a word or a line of Latin (or, after ~E, a word in {language}).
text.tr: Scribe verbum vel lineam Latinam (vel, post ~E, verbum {language}).

text.en: In the parameter dialogues, ? explains each setting.
text.tr: In dialogis parametrorum, ? quamlibet optionem explicat.

text.en: Up and Down bring back earlier searches (also those of earlier sessions).
text.tr: Up et Down reducunt inquisitiones priores (etiam illas sessionum preteritarum).

text.en: An empty line twice, or Ctrl-D, quits; Ctrl-C stops what is being done.
text.tr: Linea vacua bis scripta, vel Ctrl-D, programma claudit; Ctrl-C sistit quod fit.

text.en: py-words: a Latin-English-Latin and Latin-Spanish-Latin dictionary that analyses inflected Latin words (its starting point was William Whitaker's WORDS). With no arguments it is interactive.
text.tr: py-words: dictionarium Latino-Anglico-Latinum et Latino-Hispanico-Latinum quod verba Latina flexa resolvit (initium eius fuit WORDS Guillelmi Whitaker). Sine argumentis est interlocutorium.

text.en: In interactive mode, type ? for help.
text.tr: In modo interlocutorio, scribe ? pro auxilio.

text.en: for a word that finds nothing, show the results of its near spellings (or not, with --no-fuzzy); this time only (the setting is fuzzy_search)

text.en: The results are those of words.py (in colour, if the terminal has colours and $NO_COLOR is not set), or with F8 the entries of Logeion for the lemmas of the words (it needs the internet); the settings, the configuration file and the history of the searches are shared with it and the window. (On Windows, curses needs the windows-curses package.)
text.tr: Inventa sunt ea ipsius words.py (colorata, si terminale colores habet et $NO_COLOR non est posita), vel per F8 articuli Logeion pro lemmatibus verborum (interrete requirit); optiones, fasciculus configurationis et historia inquisitionum cum ipso et cum fenestra communia sunt. (In Windows, curses requirit fasciculum windows-curses.)

Nothing is written until the file is saved; the first save keeps the original as dictionary.xml.bak (and so for the file of the language of the meanings, in languages/, if one is chosen). Leaving an entry whose changes were not applied asks what to do with them. (On Windows, curses needs the windows-curses package; the window editor, words_edit_gui.py, needs nothing.)

Quere scribe formam Latinam, radicem vel verbum significationum, et Enter Index Up/Down ad articulum eligendum, Enter ad ipsum emendandum Forma Up/Down inter campos; scribe in campis textus; in campo cum electionibus, Left/Right ipsum mutant et Enter omnes enumerat
F3 / Ctrl-A applicare mutationes (vel addere articulum novum) F4 / Ctrl-N articulus novus F5 / Ctrl-D articulus novus huic similis F6 / Ctrl-T probare verbum F8 / Ctrl-K delere articulum F7 / Ctrl-L lingua significationum que preter Anglicam emendatur F2 / Ctrl-S servare fasciculum (mutationibus prius applicatis) F10 / Ctrl-Q exire Tab area sequens Ctrl-F querere
Nichil scribitur donec fasciculus servetur; prima servatio retinet originale tamquam dictionary.xml.bak (et similiter fasciculum lingue significationum, in languages/, si aliqua electa est). Si relinquitur articulus cuius mutationes non sunt applicate, queritur quid de eis fiat. (In Windows, curses requirit fasciculum windows-curses; editor in fenestra, words_edit_gui.py, nullo eget.)

text.en: http://127.0.0.1:8000/ the search page http://127.0.0.1:8000/?q=amicus+est a search (Latin to English) http://127.0.0.1:8000/?q=friend&lang=en a search (English to Latin)
text.tr: http://127.0.0.1:8000/ pagina inquisitionis http://127.0.0.1:8000/?q=amicus+est inquisitio (Latine → Anglice) http://127.0.0.1:8000/?q=friend&lang=en inquisitio (Anglice → Latine)

text.tr: (lang= lingua significationum, en vel es ..., pro inquisitione ab ea in Latinum.)

text.en: The results are those of words.py; the settings, the configuration file and the history of the searches are shared with it, the window and the terminal. The dictionary is read again when an editor changes it.
text.tr: Inventa sunt ea ipsius words.py; optiones, fasciculus configurationis et historia inquisitionum communia sunt cum eo, cum fenestra et cum terminali. Dictionarium iterum legitur cum editor ipsum mutat.

text.en: Only this computer can reach the server, unless --host says otherwise (--host 0.0.0.0: every computer that can reach this one, as a phone on the same network). There are no passwords, so do that only on a network you trust; the dictionary cannot be edited from the browser.
text.tr: Solum hoc computatrum servitrum attingere potest, nisi --host aliud dicat (--host 0.0.0.0: omne computatrum quod hoc attingere potest, ut telephonum in eodem rete). Nulla sunt verba secreta; ideo hoc fiat tantum in rete fido; dictionarium ex navigatro emendari non potest.

{name} {version}, a Latin dictionary by Nicolas Vaughan {url} Started from WORDS by William Whitaker (1936-2010), in the Ada version at https://github.com/mk270/whitakers-words; code and data redesigned, with a new English dictionary (Lewis and Short) and two new Spanish ones (Echave-Sustaeta and De Miguel). Sources of the dictionary: WORDS, by William Whitaker; R. E. Latham, Revised Medieval Latin Word-List (medieval words, senses and spellings); J. Echave-Sustaeta, Lengua latina. Vocabulario básico (Latin-Spanish); C. T. Lewis and C. Short, A Latin Dictionary (rare words and names, English definitions; text of the Perseus Digital Library, CC BY-SA 4.0); R. de Miguel and the Marqués de Morante, Nuevo diccionario latino- español etimológico, 1867 (rare words and proper names, Latin-Spanish); Collatinus, by Yves Ouvrard and Philippe Verkerk (long vowels). Code © 2026 Nicolas Vaughan (nicolasvaughan@proton.me), under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later (see LICENCE.txt). The data of WORDS, by William Whitaker, are free for any use. The Spanish meanings come from De Miguel and Echave-Sustaeta; for the words that neither has, they were translated from the English. The English meanings of the words taken from De Miguel were translated from his Spanish.
text.tr: {name} {version}, dictionarium Latinum a Nicolao Vaughan factum {url} Initium sumpsit ex WORDS Guillelmi Whitaker (1936-2010), in versione Ada apud https://github.com/mk270/whitakers-words; codex et data denuo composita, cum novo dictionario Anglico (Lewis et Short) et duobus novis Hispanicis (Echave-Sustaeta et De Miguel). Fontes dictionarii: WORDS, Guillelmi Whitaker; R. E. Latham, Revised Medieval Latin Word-List (verba, sensus et orthographie mediei evi); J. Echave-Sustaeta, Lengua latina. Vocabulario básico (Latino- Hispanicum); C. T. Lewis et C. Short, A Latin Dictionary (verba rara et nomina, definitiones Anglice; textus Perseus Digital Library, CC BY-SA 4.0); R. de Miguel et Marchio de Morante, Nuevo diccionario latino- español etimológico, 1867 (verba rara et nomina propria, Latino- Hispanicum); Collatinus, Yvonis Ouvrard et Philippi Verkerk (vocales longe). Codex © 2026 Nicolas Vaughan (nicolasvaughan@proton.me), sub licentia GNU General Public License, versione 3 vel posteriore (vide LICENCE.txt). Data ipsius WORDS, Guillelmi Whitaker, ad omnem usum libera sunt. Significationes Hispanice veniunt ex De Miguel et Echave-Sustaeta; pro verbis que neuter habet, ex Anglico translate sunt. Significationes Anglice verborum ex De Miguel sumptorum ex Hispanico eius translate sunt.

text.en: The program started from WORDS, by William Whitaker (1936-2010), but both its code and its data have been redesigned, and it now includes a new English dictionary (Lewis and Short) and two new Spanish ones (Echave-Sustaeta and De Miguel), besides other works. R. E. Latham, Revised Medieval Latin Word-List from British and Irish Sources, gave medieval senses, words and spellings (source code M). J. Echave-Sustaeta, Lengua latina. Vocabulario básico, gave senses and words, in English and in Spanish (source code A). Lewis and Short, A Latin Dictionary, in the text of the Perseus Digital Library (CC BY-SA 4.0), gave some 8,400 rare words and names that WORDS did not have (source code S, as other entries of WORDS taken from it), and the English definitions of some 31,000 entries. R. de Miguel and the Marqués de Morante, Nuevo diccionario latino-español etimológico (1867), gave some 25,000 words and proper names that WORDS did not have, and the Spanish meanings of some 49,000 entries (source code m); Echave-Sustaeta gave those of the entries De Miguel does not have, and the other Spanish meanings are translations. Collatinus, by Yves Ouvrard and Philippe Verkerk, gave the long vowels of the stems and endings, and some abbreviations (source code H). Collatinus, in its turn, made its lexicon with the help of the dictionaries of Gaffiot, Jeanneau, Du Cange and Lewis and Short, among others; the README names all the sources and people it thanks.
text.tr: Programma initium sumpsit ex WORDS, Guillelmi Whitaker (1936-2010), sed et codex eius et data denuo composita sunt, et nunc continet novum dictionarium Anglicum (Lewis et Short) et duo nova Hispanica (Echave-Sustaeta et De Miguel), preter alia opera. R. E. Latham, Revised Medieval Latin Word-List from British and Irish Sources, dedit sensus, verba et orthographias mediei evi (nota fontis M). J. Echave-Sustaeta, Lengua latina. Vocabulario básico, dedit sensus et verba, Anglice et Hispanice (nota fontis A). Lewis et Short, A Latin Dictionary, in textu Perseus Digital Library (CC BY-SA 4.0), dedit circiter 8.400 verba rara et nomina que WORDS non habebat (nota fontis S, sicut alii articuli ipsius WORDS ex eo sumpti), et definitiones Anglicas circiter 31.000 articulorum. R. de Miguel et Marchio de Morante, Nuevo diccionario latino-español etimológico (1867), dedit circiter 25.000 verba et nomina propria que WORDS non habebat, et significationes Hispanicas circiter 49.000 articulorum (nota fontis m); Echave-Sustaeta dedit eas articulorum quos De Miguel non habet, et cetere significationes Hispanice sunt translationes. Collatinus, Yvonis Ouvrard et Philippi Verkerk, dedit vocales longas radicum et terminationum, et quasdam abbreviationes (nota fontis H). Collatinus autem lexicon suum fecit cum auxilio dictionariorum Gaffiot, Jeanneau, Du Cange et Lewis et Short, inter alia; README nominat omnes fontes et personas quibus gratias agit.

The look of the windows and the web page: dark_mode = true for dark, false for light (none: the web page follows the system). Also changed with the moon (or sun) in the window and on the web page.
text.tr: Aspectus fenestrarum et pagine interretialis: dark_mode = true pro obscuro, false pro lucido (nullum: pagina interretialis sequitur systema). Mutatur etiam per lunam (vel solem) in fenestra et in pagina interretiali.

text.en: show the help: how to search and read the results, and exit
text.tr: ostende auxilium: quomodo queratur et inventa legantur, et exi

text.en: the help: how to search and read the results
text.tr: auxilium: quomodo queratur et inventa legantur

text.en: words.py --help lists the options of the command line.

{name} is a Latin dictionary that knows Latin grammar: it analyses a Latin word into the dictionary entries and the forms it can be, with their meanings, and finds the Latin for a word of the language of the meanings.
text.tr: {name} est dictionarium Latinum quod grammaticam Latinam novit: resolvit verbum Latinum in articulos dictionarii et formas quas esse potest, cum significationibus suis, et invenit quid Latine dicatur verbum lingue significationum.

text.en: Type a Latin word, or a whole line of Latin, and look it up: each word is analysed in turn. Capitals do not matter, nor do u and v, or i and j (iulius, Julius and IVLIVS are the same word), nor long marks and other accents: amīcus is amicus, and cælum is caelum.
text.tr: Scribe verbum Latinum, vel totam lineam Latinam, et quere: quodlibet verbum suo ordine resolvitur. Nichil refert de litteris maiusculis, nec de u et v, nec de i et j (iulius, Julius et IVLIVS sunt idem verbum), nec de signis quantitatis et aliis accentibus: amīcus est amicus, et cælum est caelum.

text.en: In the other direction, from the language of the meanings to Latin, type one word and, if you like, a part of speech after it (friend N, friend ADJ; the parts of speech are N, PRON, ADJ, NUM, ADV, V, PREP, CONJ and INTERJ): the Latin entries whose meanings have that word are listed, the best first.
text.tr: In altera directione, a lingua significationum in Latinum, scribe unum verbum et, si placet, partem orationis post ipsum (friend N, friend ADJ; partes orationis sunt N, PRON, ADJ, NUM, ADV, V, PREP, CONJ et INTERJ): enumerantur articuli Latini quorum significationes illud verbum habent, optimi primo.

text.en: When a word finds nothing as it is typed, the program tries other spellings (medieval ones, syncope, two words written as one ...) and says what it did. With the fuzzy search (on as usual), a word that still finds nothing is followed by the results of its near spellings: amicuss finds amicus. Unknown words with a capital are taken as names, and left alone.
text.tr: Cum verbum, sicut scriptum est, nichil invenit, programma temptat alias orthographias (mediei evi, syncopen, duo verba tamquam unum scripta ...) et dicit quid fecerit. Cum inquisitione approximata (que communiter agit), verbum quod adhuc nichil invenit sequuntur inventa orthographiarum vicinarum: amicuss invenit amicus. Verba ignota cum littera maiuscula habentur pro nominibus, et relinquuntur.

text.en: Type in the box at the top and press Enter, or "Look up"; the arrow at the right of the box lists the earlier searches.
text.tr: Scribe in area superiori et preme Enter, vel "Quere"; sagitta ad dexteram aree enumerat inquisitiones priores.

text.en: "Latin → …" and "… → Latin" choose the direction of the search, "Meanings in" the language of the meanings, and "Fuzzy search", beside it, whether a word that finds nothing is followed by its near spellings. The menus have the rest: Dictionary (the dictionary editor, greyed out where the dictionary cannot be written to, as in the AppImage; and the other settings, each with its help), Edit (cut, copy and paste), View (find in the results, the size of the text, the fonts, dark mode) and Help (this text, and the version and the credits).
text.tr: "Latine → …" et "… → Latine" eligunt directionem inquisitionis, "Significationes" linguam significationum, et "Inquisitio approximata", iuxta, utrum verbum quod nichil invenit sequantur orthographie vicine. Tabelle habent cetera: Dictionarium (editor dictionarii, cinereus ubi dictionarium scribi non potest, ut in AppImage; et cetere optiones, queque cum auxilio suo), Emendatio (excidere, transcribere et inserere), Aspectus (querere in inventis, magnitudo textus, typi litterarum, modus obscurus) et Auxilium (hic textus, et versio et nomina auctorum).

text.en: In the results, click the first word of an entry to look it up, or double-click any word (a word of the meanings is looked up in Latin). Point at the codes in brackets or at an analysis (GEN.PL) to see what they mean. A right click copies or looks up a word, and Ctrl and F finds a text in the results.
text.tr: In inventis, preme primum verbum articuli ut queratur, vel duplici pressu quodlibet verbum (verbum significationum queritur in Latino). Indica notas inter uncos vel analysim (GEN.PL) ut videas quid significent. Pressus dexter verbum transcribit vel querit, et Ctrl et F textum in inventis querit.

text.en: Ctrl and + or − make the text larger or smaller (Ctrl and 0: as usual), and the moon at the bottom right makes the window dark (a sun, then, makes it light again).
text.tr: Ctrl et + vel − textum maiorem vel minorem faciunt (Ctrl et 0: ut consuetum), et luna in imo ad dexteram fenestram obscurat (sol deinde eam iterum illuminat).

text.en: Type in the box at the top and press Enter, or "Look up"; the two choices below it give the direction of the search, "Meanings in" the language of the meanings, and "Fuzzy search" whether a word that finds nothing is followed by its near spellings.
text.tr: Scribe in area superiori et preme Enter, vel "Quere"; due electiones infra dant directionem inquisitionis, "Significationes" linguam significationum, et "Inquisitio approximata" utrum verbum quod nichil invenit sequantur orthographie vicine.

text.en: The first word of each entry of the results is a link to its own search, and every search has its own address, which can be bookmarked. The moon makes the page dark, and the sun light again. At the foot, "Earlier searches" lists the recent ones, "Settings" has the other settings (each with its help), "Help" is this text and "About" shows the version and the credits.
text.tr: Primum verbum cuiuslibet articuli inventorum est nexus ad suam inquisitionem, et quelibet inquisitio suam inscriptionem habet, que inter signa libri servari potest. Luna paginam obscurat, et sol iterum illuminat. In imo, "Inquisitiones priores" enumerat recentes, "Optiones" habet ceteras optiones (quamque cum auxilio suo), "Auxilium" est hic textus et "De programmate" ostendit versionem et nomina auctorum.

text.en: The first line is the word looked up. Each entry it can be follows, indented.
text.tr: Prima linea est verbum quesitum. Sequitur, cum indentatione, quilibet articulus quem esse potest.

text.en: The first line of an entry has its dictionary form (the principal parts: amicus, amici), its part of speech and its grammar in words (noun, 2nd declension, masculine), the codes in brackets ([XXXBO], see below) and, for some entries, their age or frequency in words (archaic, lesser ...).
text.tr: Prima linea articuli habet formam dictionarii (partes principales: amicus, amici), partem orationis et grammaticam verbis expressam (noun, 2nd declension, masculine), notas inter uncos ([XXXBO], vide infra) et, pro quibusdam articulis, etatem vel frequentiam verbis expressam (archaic, lesser ...).

text.en: The next line is the meaning. Its senses are separated by semicolons, the commonest first; a slash separates alternatives (counselor/courtier), and parentheses give the context. [en] before a meaning says that it is not translated, and is given in English.
text.tr: Linea sequens est significatio. Eius sensus per punctum et virgulam separantur, communissimo primo; virgula obliqua separat res alternas (counselor/courtier), et parentheses dant contextum. [en] ante significationem dicit quod non est translata, sed Anglice datur.

text.en: Then come the forms the word can be: the stem and the ending, separated by a hyphen (amīc-ōrum, with the long vowels marked), and what the form is, in the abbreviations listed below (GEN.PL: genitive plural) or, with the setting use_glosses off, in words. One spelling can be several forms: the amīc-ōrum of the adjective is GEN.PL.M and GEN.PL.N.
text.tr: Deinde veniunt forme quas verbum esse potest: radix et terminatio, per lineolam separate (amīc-ōrum, cum vocalibus longis notatis), et que forma sit, per abbreviationes infra enumeratas (GEN.PL: genitivus pluralis) vel, optione use_glosses ablata, verbis. Eadem scriptura potest esse plures forme: amīc-ōrum adiectivi est GEN.PL.M et GEN.PL.N.

text.en: A line before an entry may say how the word was found: a prefix, a suffix or an enclitic (-que, -ne, -ve) that was taken off, with its meaning, or a spelling trick (spelling: ...), with a sentence on what was done.
text.tr: Linea ante articulum potest dicere quomodo verbum inventum sit: prefixum, suffixum vel encliticum (-que, -ne, -ve) quod ablatum est, cum significatione sua, vel artificium orthographie (spelling: ...), cum sententia de eo quod factum est.

text.en: Notes in parentheses: (unknown), for a word that was not found; (near spellings: ...), before the results of its near spellings; (less likely forms are not shown), when the setting trim_output left some out. From the language of the meanings: (no match), (near words: ...) and, after the best six entries, (... more not shown).
text.tr: Annotationes inter parentheses: (unknown), pro verbo quod non est inventum; (near spellings: ...), ante inventa orthographiarum vicinarum; (less likely forms are not shown), cum optio trim_output quedam omisit. A lingua significationum: (no match), (near words: ...) et, post sex optimos articulos, (... more not shown).

text.en: The five letters in brackets after an entry say when, where, how often and on whose authority the word is used, in this order: its age, its area (the subject it belongs to), its region, its frequency and its source. X says that there is nothing particular to say: in use throughout, general, everywhere, or not known. So the [{codes}] of amicus is read:
text.tr: Quinque littere inter uncos post articulum dicunt quando, ubi, quam sepe et qua auctoritate verbum adhibeatur, hoc ordine: etas eius, materia (res ad quam pertinet), regio, frequentia et fons. X dicit nichil singulare esse dicendum: in usu per omnes etates, generale, ubique, vel ignotum. Sic [{codes}] vocabuli amicus legitur:

text.en: The forms are written with the abbreviations of the Leipzig Glossing Rules, joined by full stops (GEN.PL, 1SG.PRF.ACT.IND); those marked * are not in the Leipzig list. They are kept in data/gloss.xml, where they can be changed.
text.tr: Forme scribuntur abbreviationibus regularum glossandi Lipsiensium (Leipzig Glossing Rules), punctis iunctis (GEN.PL, 1SG.PRF.ACT.IND); que signo * notantur non sunt in catalogo Lipsiensi. Servantur in data/gloss.xml, ubi mutari possunt.

text.en: Each setting has its own help: in the Settings of the window and the web page, in F3 of the terminal, and with ? in the # and ! dialogues of the command line. The parameters are for everyone, the developer modes for special purposes; the programs share them.
text.tr: Quelibet optio suum auxilium habet: in Optionibus fenestre et pagine interretialis, in F3 terminalis, et cum ? in dialogis # et ! linee mandatorum. Parametra sunt pro omnibus, modi elaboratoris ad usus speciales; programmata ea communia habent.

text.en: Double-click any word of the results to look it up (a word of the meanings is looked up in Latin), and point at the codes in brackets or at an analysis (GEN.PL), or tap them, to see what they mean.
text.tr: Preme bis quodlibet verbum inventorum ut queratur (verbum significationum in Latinum queritur), et murem pone super notas inter uncos vel super analysim (GEN.PL), vel eas tange, ut videas quid significent.

text.en: <stems> must have from one to four stems
text.tr: <stems> debet habere ab una ad quattuor radices

text.en: the stem "{text}" may only contain letters, with long marks on vowels (ā), or be -
text.tr: radix "{text}" non potest continere nisi litteras, cum signis longitudinis in vocalibus (ā), vel esse -

text.en: there is no entry with the id {id}: these stems are not used
text.tr: nullus est articulus cum id {id}: he radices non adhibentur

text.en: "{marked}" is not the stem "{stem}" of the entry: it is not used
text.tr: "{marked}" non est radix "{stem}" articuli: non adhibetur

text.en: Always say in words when a word or form was used (archaic, classical, medieval ...) and how frequent it is, not only when it is unusual.
text.tr: Semper verbis dic quando verbum vel forma adhibita sit (archaica, classica, mediei evi ...) et quam frequens sit, non solum cum insolita est.

text.en: An entry can have more than one source: then the others follow the five letters, each after a + ([XXXCO+M] is also from source M). The age, when it is known, and the frequency, when it is lesser or rarer, are also given in words after the codes (archaic, lesser ...). The parameter show_codes hides the codes, and the dictionary editors explain each code of an entry as it is edited.
text.tr: Articulus potest habere plures fontes: tunc ceteri sequuntur quinque litteras, quilibet post + ([XXXCO+M] etiam ex fonte M est). Etas, cum noscitur, et frequentia, cum minor vel rarior est, etiam verbis dantur post notas (archaic, lesser ...). Parametrum show_codes notas occultat, et editores dictionarii quamlibet notam articuli explicant dum emendatur.

text.en: Leave out the least likely results: forms that are only possible in theory, and archaic or uncommon ones when more common results were found. A note says when something was left out. In the search to Latin, show only the best six results. Poets use unusual words and forms, so these can be trimmed wrongly.
text.tr: Omitte inventa minus probabilia: formas que solum in theoria possibiles sunt, et archaicas vel insolitas cum communiora inventa sunt. Annotatio dicit cum aliquid omissum est. In inquisitione in Latinum, ostende sola sex optima inventa. Poete verbis et formis insolitis utuntur, et ideo he perperam resecari possunt.

text.en: Mark the long vowels of the stems and endings in the forms (amīc-ōrum), where they are known. Vowels long before two consonants are not marked, but for those before ns and nf.
text.tr: Nota vocales longas radicum et terminationum in formis (amīc-ōrum), ubi noscuntur. Vocales longe ante duas consonantes non notantur, preter eas que sunt ante ns et nf.

text.en: Show which dictionary (general or special) each entry is from, and its number in that file.
text.tr: Ostende ex quo dictionario (generali vel speciali) quilibet articulus sit, et numerum eius in illo fasciculo.

text.en: When a word is still not found, try other spellings (ae for e, ph for f, assimilated prefixes ...) and two words written as one. Such results are marked as such.
text.tr: Cum verbum adhuc non invenitur, tempta alias orthographias (ae pro e, ph pro f, prefixa assimilata ...) et duo verba tamquam unum scripta. Talia inventa ut talia notantur.

text.en: With trim_output, leave out also medieval forms when others were found.
text.tr: Cum trim_output, omitte etiam formas mediei evi cum alie invente sunt.

text.en: With use_tricks, also try medieval spellings (e for ae, y for i, michi for mihi, single for doubled consonants ...), also for a word that is found: its e may be ae or oe (queruntur, of queror, is also quaeruntur, of quaero).
text.tr: Cum use_tricks, tempta etiam orthographias mediei evi (e pro ae, y pro i, michi pro mihi, consonantes simplices pro geminatis ...), etiam pro verbo quod invenitur: eius e potest esse ae vel oe (queruntur, a queror, est etiam quaeruntur, a quaero).

text.en: Changes are kept in this browser (in its cookies).
text.tr: Mutationes in hoc navigatro servantur (in crustulis eius).

text.en: as on a web server for everyone: each visitor with their own settings and history, in cookies
text.tr: sicut in servitro interretiali omnibus aperto: quilibet visitator cum suis optionibus et historia, in crustulis

text.en: On a web server open to everyone (as PythonAnywhere), the application is public_app(): each visitor's settings, languages, look and earlier searches are kept in the cookies of their browser, and nothing is saved on the server (--public tries it here).
text.tr: In servitro interretiali omnibus aperto (ut PythonAnywhere), applicatio est public_app(): optiones, lingue, aspectus et inquisitiones priores cuiuslibet visitatoris servantur in crustulis navigatri sui, et nichil in servitro servatur (--public hic ipsum temptat).

text.en: The results were copied, if the terminal lets programs use the clipboard.
text.tr: Inventa transcripta sunt, si terminale programmatibus tabulam communem adhibere permittit.

text.en: "Search in" chooses where the words are looked up: Local, this dictionary, or Logeion (logeion.uchicago.edu), the dictionaries of the University of Chicago (Lewis and Short, Georges, Gaffiot, DMLBS, Du Cange …). Logeion does not analyse inflected forms, so each word is analysed here first, and the analysis is shown, without its meanings, before Logeion's entries for its lemmas. It searches in Latin only: the other direction, the language of the meanings and the fuzzy search are greyed out meanwhile. The list beside "Search in" chooses Logeion's dictionary, or all of them. In the entries, a link to another word of Logeion looks it up, and the other links open in a new tab.
text.tr: "Quere in" eligit ubi verba querantur: Hic, hoc dictionarium, vel Logeion (logeion.uchicago.edu), dictionaria Universitatis Chicagiensis (Lewis and Short, Georges, Gaffiot, DMLBS, Du Cange …). Logeion formas flexas non resolvit; ideo quodlibet verbum hic primo resolvitur, et analysis ostenditur, sine significationibus suis, ante articulos Logeion pro lemmatibus eius. In solo Latino querit: altera directio, lingua significationum et inquisitio approximata interim obscurantur. Index iuxta "Quere in" eligit dictionarium Logeion, vel omnia. In articulis, nexus ad aliud verbum Logeion ipsum querit, et ceteri nexus in nova pagina navigatri aperiuntur.

text.en: (Logeion is asked only for the first {count} words.)

"Search in" chooses where the words are looked up: Local, this dictionary, or Logeion (logeion.uchicago.edu), the dictionaries of the University of Chicago (Lewis and Short, Georges, Gaffiot, DMLBS, Du Cange …), which needs the internet. Logeion does not analyse inflected forms, so each word is analysed here and Logeion is asked for its lemmas (arma: armum and armo; and arma itself, a headword of Lewis and Short's); the analysis is shown first, without its meanings (dixi: dix-ī 1SG.PRF.ACT.IND), and then Logeion's entries. It searches in Latin only: the other direction, the language of the meanings, the fuzzy search and the dictionary editor (which edits this dictionary) are greyed out meanwhile. The list beside "Search in" chooses Logeion's dictionary (Lewis and Short, Gaffiot …) or all of them; the short definition, the frequency and the examples are shown with any. Its links to other words look them up; the others open in the browser. In the terminal, F8 changes the source and F5 the dictionary; on the command line, --logeion and --dictionary, and in interactive mode ~G and ~D. The source, the dictionary and the direction last chosen are kept for the next start.
text.tr: "Quere in" eligit ubi verba querantur: Hic, hoc dictionarium, vel Logeion (logeion.uchicago.edu), dictionaria Universitatis Chicagiensis (Lewis and Short, Georges, Gaffiot, DMLBS, Du Cange …), quod interrete requirit. Logeion formas flexas non resolvit; ideo quodlibet verbum hic resolvitur et a Logeion petuntur lemmata eius (arma: armum et armo; et ipsum arma, lemma Lewis et Short); primo ostenditur analysis, sine significationibus suis (dixi: dix-ī 1SG.PRF.ACT.IND), et deinde articuli Logeion. In solo Latino querit: altera directio, lingua significationum, inquisitio approximata et editor dictionarii (qui hoc dictionarium emendat) interim obscurantur. Index iuxta "Quere in" eligit dictionarium Logeion (Lewis and Short, Gaffiot …) vel omnia; definitio brevis, frequentia et exempla cum quolibet ostenduntur. Nexus eius ad alia verba ipsa querunt; ceteri in navigatro aperiuntur. In terminali, F8 fontem mutat et F5 dictionarium; in linea mandatorum, --logeion et --dictionary, et in modo interlocutorio ~G et ~D. Fons, dictionarium et directio ultimo electa pro proximo initio servantur.

text.en: Where the programs look words up: source = "local" (this dictionary) or "logeion" (the entries of Logeion for the lemmas of the words, which needs the internet); and dictionary = "all" or the code of the only dictionary of Logeion shown (dmlbs, as usual; ls, gaffiot …; words.py --dictionaries lists them). Kept when changed with "Search in" and the list beside it in the window and on the web page, F8 and F5 in the terminal, and ~G and ~D in interactive mode; --logeion, --local and --dictionary change them for one run.
text.tr: Ubi programmata verba querant: source = "local" (hoc dictionarium) vel "logeion" (articuli Logeion pro lemmatibus verborum, quod interrete requirit); et dictionary = "all" vel nota solius dictionarii Logeion quod ostenditur (dmlbs, ut solet; ls, gaffiot …; words.py --dictionaries ea enumerat). Servantur cum mutantur per "Quere in" et indicem iuxta ipsum in fenestra et in pagina interretiali, per F8 et F5 in terminali, et per ~G et ~D in modo interlocutorio; --logeion, --local et --dictionary ea mutant pro una vice.

text.en: The direction of the last search, for the next start: to_latin = true (from the language of the meanings to Latin) or false. Kept when changed in the window, with F2 in the terminal and with ~E and ~L in interactive mode.
text.tr: Directio ultime inquisitionis, pro proximo initio: to_latin = true (a lingua significationum in Latinum) vel false. Servatur cum mutatur in fenestra, per F2 in terminali et per ~E et ~L in modo interlocutorio.
--local non potest simul esse cum --logeion vel --dictionary
